page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-1000s-amd is an AMD EPYC-based server instance belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provided locally via a 1000 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The x86_64 CPU architecture supports AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong compute and memory performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance registers in the top 10% tier, while multi-core performance falls within the top 25% tier. Passmark CPU and memory scores are highly competitive, with the memory score reaching the top 10% tier. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 346.3 GB/sec, and write bandwidth is measured at 164.36 GB/sec. For database and key-value workloads, the server achieves 76.91 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, though Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput remain in the middle 50% average tier.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a compute-heavy design, making this instance highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per core may act as a bottleneck for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. The server demonstrates strong capabilities in lightweight machine learning, achieving top-tier text generation speeds of 43.67 tokens per second on a 7B LLM model. This profile is well-suited for multi-threaded decompression, compute-intensive web applications, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference tasks.
